text:
jason: Putting a draft out — we need a compact representation for model-specific quotas that we can both enforce at the edge and expose in the console. My working idea: a quota matrix keyed by org/key + model-family tier with separate burst credit buckets. Sharing a rough example and follow-up questions.

maria: This is great. Can you paste the example? need to see shape for the UI column names.

jason: Sure — example policy payload:

```
{
  "org_id": "acme",
  "key_id": "k_123",
  "quotas": {
    "tiny": {"rps": 50, "burst": 100},
    "base": {"rps": 20, "burst": 40},
    "large": {"rps": 5,  "burst": 10},
    "xlarge": {"rps": 1,  "burst": 2}
  },
  "burst_window_secs": 60
}
```

jason: Enforcement would decrement per-key family bucket on request. If family bucket empty, fallback to per-org generic bucket or return 429 depending on policy.

suresh: Two immediate thoughts: telemetry and backlog. We should emit events: `quota.check`, `quota.consume`, `quota.replenish`, and include model_family in tags. That lets us chart per-family burn rates. Also, is burst implemented as token-bucket per family or as a shared org-level credit?

jason: Prefer token-bucket per family with optional `share_with_org` flag to let small teams borrow from org pool. Default is isolated per-key to prevent noisy neighbors.

nina: UI: we can't show too many columns for each family on small screens. Proposal: show summarized tiers in the table (tiny/base/large) and a collapsible detail panel that shows burst and replenishment rate. Also add an inline tooltip "effective rps" that accounts for burst smoothing.

ryan: UX note — when a quota change is rolled out, teams expect immediate enforcement but also a grace period. Can we wire the rollout system so changes have 3 modes: `preview` (no enforcement, only telemetry), `soft` (throttle with headers and logs), `hard` (enforce 429)? This mirrors feature-flag rollout patterns.

jason: Agree. We can append a `mode` field to the policy and surface it in console with a prominent warning if not `hard`.

maria: Implementation Qs: how do proxies pick the family? by model metadata? by API param? We have to be explicit to avoid misclassification when users supply custom container models.

suresh: We should use model reference metadata (model.family or model.size) included in the routing header. For user-uploaded/custom models, onboarding must include a required `family` tag. If missing, default route to `base` and emit a warning metric.

nina: For the console, we also need an override UI to set temporary emergency increases for a key/org. Keep audit log of who changed it and add a TTL so it auto-reverts.

jason: Good call. Audit + TTL + revert should be enforced server-side. Also add an API endpoint `POST /quota/override` that takes {key_id, delta, ttl_seconds, reason}. ops-bot can detect overrides > X and create incident.

ops-bot: Note: I can emit a channel alert when `override` is used and include the diff. Want me to wire that now?

ryan: Yes please, have it post to #incidents and #eng-platform with metadata. Also include a lightweight rendered table in the message.

maria: Back to enforcement: what happens when model variants share the same family but have very different token cost per response? Throttling on RPS alone may favor high-cost models.

jason: We should support quota units beyond RPS: tokens_per_minute or a weighted unit. Proposal: each model_family policy can include `unit = [requests|tokens|cost_units]` and a `weight` multiplier. The runtime should deduct `weight * cost_estimate` for each call.

suresh: We'll need runtime estimates: either static model token cost heuristics (avg tokens per call for a family) or the agent that declares predicted cost. We already have telemetry to sample actual token usage; use that to refine weights.

nina: Console needs to show both RPS and token burn graphs. Also an "effective budget" calc that translates quotas to estimated number of typical calls per day using recent avg tokens.

jason: For rollouts: when moving a policy from `preview`->`soft`, emit a `quota.rollout` event and auto-schedule an audit after 24h to check for error/latency regressions.

maria: Edge-case: what if model_family name changes during a model update? We should version mapping and support aliasing so old keys don't suddenly get new limits.

jason: Add `family_aliases` in the model registry and tie quota policies to family IDs not labels. Console can render current labels but backend binds to IDs.

suresh: Implementation timeline suggestion: week 1 — policy schema + API + telemetry events; week 2 — enforcement in proxy with simple RPS/burst token-buckets; week 3 — console table + override UI + rollout modes; week 4 — weights/tokens support + sampling-based weight tuning. Thoughts?

maria: That seems reasonable. I'd bump week 2 to include shared org pool capability as an optional flag since lots of customers ask for borrowing.

jason: Okay bumping. I'll write up a spec PR with the schema and examples. Link when ready.

nina: One last pic: default policy set for new orgs should be conservative and marked as editable. Also add an onboarding check to surface families detected in their first 24h of traffic so they can tune quotas.

jason: Great. Action items: (1) jason: draft spec PR, (2) suresh: telemetry event schema, (3) nina: console wireframe for matrix + collapse, (4) maria: confirm legal/enterprise constraints for auto-borrowing. I'll ping when PR is up.

maria: Thanks — excited to see the draft.

jason: PR: https://git.redwood/internal/infra/quota-matrix/pull/42 (draft)

suresh: I'll add initial event schema to that PR by EOD.

nina: I'll drop a Figma link in the PR comments with the table mockup.

ryan: Moving to `watching`.

maria: :thumbsup:
